Presented By
NRL Late Mail: Round 23 - Tedesco out; Metcalf, Talagi step up
The Warriors and Panthers have both been forced into changes in the halves ahead of Friday night's clash in Auckland.
Warriors playmaker Te Maire Martin suffered a hamstring injury at training and has been replaced by Luke Metcalf, while Panthers five-eighth Jack Cogger has remained in Sydney for the birth of his child, with Blaize Talagi taking his place.
Experienced prop Lindsay Collins makes his return for the Roosters in Friday night's blockbuster showdown against the Bulldogs, who welcome back Sitili Tupouniua .
Collins' last appearance was in Round 17 with the club taking a cautious approach after ongoing concussion concerns.
Tupouniua has missed five games with a hamstring injury and adds another dimension to a Bulldogs outfit flying high with six wins in their past seven matches.

NRL Casualty Ward: Surgery for McLean; Martin, Nanai hamstrung
Panthers centre Casey McLean has had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean sees three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
Andrew Webster's men will be without Te Maire Martin after he picked up a hamstring strain at training on Wednesday but gun fullback Taine Tuaupiki is set to return from a foot injury.
In Friday night's other monster showdown, the Roosters have winger Billy Smith back from illness and prop Lindsay Collins set for his first game since Round 17 after ongoing concussion issues, while the Bulldogs get star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua back from a hamstring injury.
On the negative side, James Tedesco will be given another week to overcome an ankle injury suffered in the massive win over the Cowboys.
Huge ins at South Sydney as well where skipper Cameron Murray (calf) plays his first game since Round 20 while Tallis Duncan (hamstring) and David Fifita (suspension) are also back to face the Eels.
The Storm receive a boost with five-eighth Cameron Munster returning after four games out following surgery for knee cartilage damage. Centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) also returns but Jahrome Hughes remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Roosters v Bulldogs: Tedesco sidelined; Tupouniua back on deck
The Bulldogs have come from the clouds to climb into the top eight but they get a true test of their credentials this week against the red-hot Roosters.
With wins in six of their past seven matches, the Bulldogs have jumped from 14th to eighth ahead of a monster fortnight against the Roosters and Rabbitohs.
The Roosters have put together six wins on the trot, the latest being a record-breaking demolition of the Cowboys in which Sam Walker piled on 38 points of his own, second only to Immortal Dave Brown's 45-point haul in 1935 for the most by a Rooster in a match.
With a host of attacking weapons on both sides this promises to be one of the games of the season as two powerhouse clubs square off in a potential semi-final rehearsal.
Some 22 years have passed the Roosters and Bulldogs fought out an epic grand final and the rivalry remains as strong today as it was back in 2004.

Roosters vs Bulldogs Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
August 5 th 2026, 7:15pm , By: Scooby
The second NRL game on Friday night heads to Sydney with the Roosters hosting the Bulldogs . These two sides have enjoyed a rivalry for several years and the resurgence of the Bulldogs sets the stage for another renewal of this epic contest. The Roosters will not want to give up home ground advantage without a fight and a preview of the NRL Finals could be ahead in this match. Before You Bet is here with a comprehensive look at what is ahead in this contest to assist with finding you a winner or two to get your weekend off to a good start.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Roosters vs Bulldogs Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
Roosters flexing their muscles
Traveling to Townsville to face the Cowboys, few expected the Roosters to dominate as much as they did in their 82-12 victory. With everything going their way, the Roosters took their chances and were several levels above their opponents. Credit must go to their execution, which maintain this standard for the full 80 minutes. Their dominance was something to admire; they had 64% possession, completed at 90%, made 11.1m per carry, had 679 PCM’s, and made 11 line breaks. Regardless of the circumstances, it was a warning sign of what they are capable of.
Bulldogs getting their bite back
Also experiencing a tricky road trip, the Bulldogs overcame the Storm in Melbourne 36-22. Locked up at 16-all at HT, the match was in the balance but thankfully for them, they prevailed in the second half by generating their own positive attacking momentum. With an equal share of possession and the same completion rate as their opponents (76%), their power in the middle was imperative to their success. They averaged 9.5m per carry and made 535 PCM’s, while also creating 9 line breaks. Such a level of execution had previously abandoned them. They still need to improve in some areas, missing 34 tackles and switching off defensively to concede 4 total tries.
Stats that matter
- The home team has won the past 6 games between these two sides. This sees the Roosters win 64% of games played here compared to the Bulldogs 50%.
- There is a history of close matches with 3 of the past 5 games decided by 4 points or less. This has the average margin of victory at 9.4 points. The total points scored in the same matches is 45.4.
- There is no doubt that the Roosters have been superior this season on both sides of the ball. They score 27ppg in attack and concede just 19ppg defensively. The Bulldogs average 19ppg in attack but concede 22ppg in defence.
A true test ahead
It has been smooth sailing recently for the Bulldogs, but they are about to face their toughest test. The Roosters were great last week but with everything going their way, we are yet to see them pressured relentlessly and this might be the week it comes their way. In the same breath, you cannot overlook the confidence which they are playing with. Form suggests that they are deserving of favouritism. With an extra day to prepare following a road trip, they should be primed to perform well in this game. The home side will have a defensive structure capable of combating what they see with Crichton at 5/8. This has seen the downfall of other clubs in the competition.
With the Roosters performing well, you must go looking for value if you wish to invest on this contest. The key is that the Bulldogs have an average loss margin this season of 17.1 points; with the Roosters winning by an average of 19.5 when they are victorious. Once they gather enough momentum in the middle to break down their opponents’ defensive line, they should be capable over covering the line offered.

items.body_excerpt:
Inside Critta's leadership evolution as Bulldogs eye statement win
Bulldogs captain Stephen Crichton has revealed the club's early-season struggles helped him evolve as a leader as he looks to guide the side to an unexpected finals berth.
Canterbury may be riding a wave of momentum with six wins from their past seven games, but it wasn't always so as the club battled a disappointing start to the year.
The Bulldogs slumped to 14th on the ladder after 13 rounds, as a perfect storm of injuries and rule changes combined to send the team's campaign off course.
Crichton was among the group to spend time on the sidelines but has made up for lost time as Canterbury have surged into the eight leading into Friday's blockbuster against the Roosters at Allianz Stadium.
Captain Critta seals the deal
It was an unfamiliar position for the captain to find himself in, with Crichton winning three titles at the Panthers before leading the Bulldogs to the finals in his first two years at the club.
Looking back, the skipper acknowledges it was a challenging start to the year but is confident he's come out the other side a better leader.
"It's always tough when you're losing and people are expecting wins," Crichton said. "The last couple of years we built that expectation, which is a good thing.
